subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated capacity SLOs)

Hey John — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Dedicated capacity validation: 

1) SLO targets you confirmed on the call:
   - p95 latency target (end-to-end, token streaming): 250ms for short responses (~50-150 tokens)
   - Sustained throughput: 200 requests/sec (average request size ~128 tokens)
   - Peak concurrency target: 120 concurrent sessions (user-facing chat)
   - Streaming: required (partial token streaming / SSE)

2) What we'll validate in the Dedicated capacity run:
   - GPU type comparison (A100 vs H100) for your model variant
   - Reserved throughput sizing to meet p95 under target concurrency
   - Impact of batching and KV cache behavior for chat workloads
   - Failure / fallback behavior with degraded capacity

3) Proposed timeline & next steps:
   - This week: Redwood will provide a bench plan and a list of metrics we need from your side (SRE access to sample traffic profile or replay trace). (attached: draft-map.pdf)
   - Next week: 24-48h validation run on dedicated nodes (A100 then H100) with your sample workload
   - Following run: share results and sizing recommendation (reserved throughput and autoscale buffer)

Can you confirm the SLO numbers above are correct, and whether you can provide either a traffic replay (preferred) or a small synthetic trace that matches peak patterns? Also confirm any constraints on model size/variant you want tested.

Thanks — I'll loop in Aditya for the technical bench plan and Marissa to keep timelines aligned with procurement.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated capacity SLOs)

Alex — thanks for the summary. Confirming the targets with a few clarifications: 

- p95: we would prefer to aim for 200-250ms p95 for short responses. 250ms is acceptable as an upper bound, 200ms would be ideal.
- Throughput: 200 req/s sustained is correct for our baseline. We have a burst to ~400 req/s for ~30s in peak scenarios.
- Concurrency: our important metric is concurrent interactive sessions (users) — 120 is accurate.
- Streaming: yes — critical. Users expect partial results as they type; low first-byte latency matters.

We can provide a traffic replay from our test harness (will share a signed link by EOD). The model variant for production is the 7B-optimized quantized flavor — we can also supply a saved checkpoint or container.

A couple of asks from our SRE team: please include first-byte latency (time-to-first-token) as a primary metric, and test both cold and warm KV-cache cases. Also confirm what observability (traces/metrics) Redwood will ship during the run.

John
John Doe
Sr. Engineering Manager, Acme Corp

Alex — thanks. A couple internal notes before we hand to Aditya for bench design:

- We should explicitly compare A100 (40GB or 80GB?) vs H100 performance for the 7B quantized variant, and include quantization mode (int8 vs q4f16) in the matrix. Customers often pick H100 for latency but cost can be 20-40% higher; we need to show unit economics.
- Recommend starting reserved throughput at 250 req/s to cover baseline + buffer, and validate down to 150 req/s to provide a recommended commit band.
- Add target first-byte p50/p95 in the bench plan. John asked for time-to-first-token — include that as a graph.

Aditya — can you draft the bench-plan doc and an execution checklist (test harness requirements, observability endpoints, sample load schedule)? Also include a short failover validation: drop one GPU and measure tail latency impact.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated capacity SLOs)

Thanks all — putting the technical validation plan here and next steps. High-level test matrix and deliverables below.

Validation objectives:
- Demonstrate configuration(s) of Dedicated capacity that meet Acme's p95 <= 250ms and first-byte latency targets under stated concurrency/throughput patterns.
- Provide recommended reserved throughput commit and expected cost delta between GPU types.

Bench test matrix (to be executed sequentially):
1) Model variant: Acme 7B-quantized (customer-supplied container/checkpoint)
2) Hardware: A100-80GB, H100-80GB (single-node then 2-node cluster runs)
3) Quantization modes: q4f16, int8 (where supported)
4) Batching regimes: minimal batching (streaming, batch size=1), auto-batching at 8, 16, 32
5) Concurrency profiles: steady 200 req/s, burst profile to 400 req/s for 30s every 5m, and sustained 120 concurrent sessions simulated via session-aware load generator
6) Cache states: cold (empty KV) vs warm (populated KV from 10k recent sessions)
7) Fault scenarios: single-GPU drop + auto-fallback to compatible model variant

Metrics to capture (we will stream these to your SRE endpoint or share a read-only Grafana link):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 end-to-end latency
- time-to-first-token (TTFT) p50/p95
- tokens/sec and requests/sec
- GPU utilization, memory, and per-request kernel timings
- error rate and tail spike detection flags

Deliverables and timeline:
- Today (EOD): bench-plan.docx (attached) — includes load schedule and observability endpoints
- Tomorrow: we request the traffic replay link and the model container/checkpoint. Also need any IP allowlist for our test nodes.
- Next week: 48h A100 run, 48h H100 run (staggered) — we will run identical traces and produce comparative reports
- Post-runs: detailed report with sizing recommendation (reserved throughput levels, recommended autoscale headroom), cost delta, and a short runbook for procurement/provisioning.

Attachments: bench-plan.docx, raw-results-template.csv

If that plan looks good John, please send the replay link and the model artifact to aditya_rao@redwood.com and grant read-only Grafana access to metrics@redwood.com (we'll provide the IPs to whitelist).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
